result.summary: Disconnects all connected callbacks in the `btcsignals::signal` destructor. This ensures surviving connection handles report disconnected and any captured callback state is released upon signal destruction.
result.problem: When a `connection` handle outlives its `signal`, any callback connected at the time of signal destruction remains alive with its captured state, and the surviving handle continues to report `connected() == true`.
evidence: PR description references merged PR #36011 review discussion pointing out that destroying a signal still did not disconnect callbacks automatically and that tests should cover this case
result.changed_since_previous: None; the diff matches the earlier summary.
result.card: Disconnects callbacks automatically when a signal is destroyed in btcsignals, and extends unit tests to verify cleanup. Previously, if a connection handle outlived the signal without an explicit disconnect call, callbacks remained alive with captured state and the surviving handle falsely reported connected. This resolves an edge case left over from merged PR #36011.

risk.why: A flaw during signal disconnection on destruction could trigger double-disconnects or crash during teardown of objects holding signal subscriptions.
